text: catmech R package auditable multiple imputation, prospective audit planning, measurement error modeling, downstream regression pooling. addresses situations observational cohorts, electronic health record (EHR) registries, clinical trial data contain continuous measurements subject recording errors, unit slips, transcription errors, gold-standard reference measurement audited subset records. Instead either discarding un-audited records (inflating standard errors) naively trusting recorded numbers (introducing severe attenuation bias), catmech provides: 1. Prospective Two-Phase Audit Sample Size Planning (catmech_audit_power(), catmech_audit_plan()). 2. Reference-Calibrated Imputation & Mixture Modeling (catmech_reference(), catmech_contamination(), catmech_model(), catmech_pmm()). 3. Multi-Endpoint Downstream Regression Pooling (catmech_pool_lm(), catmech_pool_glm(), catmech_pool_coxph()) Rubin combining rules, Barnard–Rubin finite-sample degrees freedom, cluster-robust sandwich covariance (CV3 jackknife linear models, Huber–White–Liang–Zeger GLMs, Lin–Wei Cox PH). 4. Side--Side Audit Strategy Comparison (catmech_compare_strategies()) evaluating validation subsamples, naive analysis, linear MI, mixture models comparative forest plots. 5. Native Base R Visualizations: Forest plots pooled models (plot.catmech_pooled_glm(), plot.catmech_pooled_coxph(), plot.catmech_pooled_lm()), strategy comparisons, PIT calibration histograms (plot.catmech_holdout_check()), recording discrepancy audits, power curves. 6. Tidyverse / broom Generics: tidy() glance() S3 methods pooled regression models. 7. title: Auditable Clinical Data Verification and Analysis with catmech
text: multi-center clinical trials, epidemiological studies, electronic health record (EHR) registries, continuous laboratory measurements (troponin, serum creatinine, viral load) frequently suffer data quality issues: Missing values due uncollected lost samples. Gross recording errors data contamination resulting transcription mistakes, assay batch errors, EHR unit conversion discrepancies. Internal reference audits secondary gold-standard measurement audited subset patient records. catmech package provides auditable framework completing contaminated measurements, checking predictive calibration, pooling downstream linear, generalized linear (GLM), survival (Cox PH) regressions Rubin’s rules Barnard–Rubin degrees freedom. also rough, unvalidated aid planning audit sizes. package outside peer review clinical validation; README gives evidence limits.

title: Auditable Clinical Data Verification and Analysis with catmech
text: simulate realistic 10-hospital clinical registry N=250N = 250 patients. patient : * audited gold-standard reference measurement (lab_true). * recorded measurement (lab_value) corrupted fraction patients. * Patient covariates (age, sex, site). * Three downstream clinical endpoints: - Continuous outcome (cardiac_index). - Binary 30-day major adverse cardiac event (mace_30d). - Time--event overall survival (time, death_event).
code: library(catmech) library(survival)  set.seed(2026) n <- 250 site <- sample(1:10, n, replace = TRUE) age <- round(rnorm(n, mean = 62, sd = 10)) sex <- sample(c("M", "F"), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.55, 0.45))  # Latent true biomarker lab_true <- rnorm(n, mean = 6.0 + 0.03 * (age - 62), sd = 1.2)  # Corrupted recorded measurement (12% gross contamination) corrupted <- rbinom(n, 1, prob = 0.12) == 1 lab_recorded <- lab_true lab_recorded[corrupted] <- lab_recorded[corrupted] + rnorm(sum(corrupted), mean = 4.5, sd = 2.0)  # Reference audit on a 25% random pilot audited <- rbinom(n, 1, prob = 0.25) == 1 lab_reference <- ifelse(audited, lab_true, NA_real_)  # Clinical outcomes cardiac_index <- 2.8 - 0.25 * lab_true + 0.01 * (age - 62) + rnorm(n, sd = 0.5) pr_mace <- plogis(-2.0 + 0.45 * (lab_true - 6.0) + 0.02 * (age - 62)) mace_30d <- rbinom(n, 1, prob = pr_mace)  # Survival times haz <- exp(0.35 * (lab_true - 6.0) + 0.02 * (age - 62)) * 0.08 surv_time <- rexp(n, rate = haz) censor_time <- runif(n, 1, 10) time <- pmin(surv_time, censor_time) death_event <- as.numeric(surv_time <= censor_time)  df <- data.frame(   patient_id = 1:n,   site = site,   age = age,   sex = factor(sex),   lab_value = lab_recorded,   lab_ref = lab_reference,   cardiac_index = cardiac_index,   mace_30d = mace_30d,   time = time,   death_event = death_event ) head(df[, c("patient_id", "site", "age", "lab_value", "lab_ref", "mace_30d")]) #>   patient_id site age lab_value lab_ref mace_30d #> 1          1    9  43  6.111779      NA        0 #> 2          2    1  66  6.970042      NA        0 #> 3          3    6  70  7.333651      NA        1 #> 4          4    4  42  5.012186      NA        0 #> 5          5    5  60  4.937939      NA        0 #> 6          6   10  52  4.324780      NA        0
